skill.displayName: Work Productivity Skillscan Security Workflow Helper

version.changelog:
- Requirement evidence updated to reflect 12 separate online signals (up from 9), underscoring broader demand.
- All documentation updated to match new evidence count.
- skill-card.md file removed for streamlined documentation.
- Minor consistency improvements in requirement description and references.

llm.summary: This skill is not malware, but its automatic activation rules are broad enough that it could affect unrelated user requests.

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions favor local-friendly workflows, templates, checklists, and small scripts; no credential use, broad file indexing, network calls, or privileged environment access is requested.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact contains Markdown documentation and one YAML agent descriptor; no executable scripts, package installs, or install-time commands were present.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill and README list broad triggers such as security, every, must, pass, before, activate, and bug fix, and agents/openai.yaml enables implicit invocation, creating a real risk of unintended routing outside the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No persistence mechanism, background worker, privilege escalation, or credential/session handling was found; the only standing behavior concern is implicit invocation.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is a workflow/checklist helper for SkillScan-style security and reliability work; that capability is coherent, but the demand framing is generic and loosely bounded.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review the activation settings before installing. The skill appears to be a documentation-only helper, but its trigger words should be narrowed or implicit invocation disabled so it only runs when you explicitly ask for SkillScan-style workflow, security-gate, or artifact-review help.
llm.findings: [SQP-1] unexpected: The scanner's activation-scope concern is supported by the artifact: multiple files use generic trigger words and the OpenAI agent config allows implicit invocation. This does not show malicious behavior, but it is overbroad for a narrowly scoped workflow helper.
